Tetris. A Soviet-designed puzzle game released in 1984, built on the mechanic of rotating and dropping geometric tetrominoes—four-square blocks—to clear horizontal lines. Simple yet infinitely replayable, it became one of the best-selling and most-played video games of all time, transcending gaming to become a cultural phenomenon. Alexey Pajitnov designed it in 1984 at the Soviet Academy of Sciences. It was released commercially on the Nintendo Game Boy in 1989, bundled with most units, driving handheld gaming adoption worldwide.

The core mechanic involves seven distinct tetromino shapes—I, O, T, S, Z, J, and L—falling from the top of a grid. Players rotate and position them to complete horizontal lines, which vanish and award points. Speed increases as the game progresses. Blocks fall faster, creating escalating difficulty and tension between strategic placement and reaction time. There is no failure state, only increasing challenge. The game became a cultural icon. The Tetris theme, based on the Russian folk song Korobeiniki, is one of the most recognizable video game pieces ever composed. The game's simple premise masks deep strategic depth.

Countless adaptations followed across platforms: Game Boy, NES, Sega Genesis, arcade cabinets, mobile phones, even Alexa devices and Glow Soccer pieces. Each generation rediscovered the game. Modern entries include Tetris Effect in 2018 with psychedelic visuals and music integration, and Tetris 99 in 2019, a battle-royale variant on Nintendo Switch where ninety-nine players compete simultaneously.

The franchise holds world records for both single-game engagement and lifetime revenue. A 2020 film dramatized the Cold War licensing battles over Tetris rights. Alexey Pajitnov was the Soviet computer scientist and original designer. Tetris represents the foundational example of elegant, endless replayability in puzzle games. Game Boy became culturally synonymous with Nintendo's handheld success, largely through Tetris. The game's theme song remains iconic enough to be recognized globally across all ages and cultures.
